findings.title: Bitwise type error ignores __name, unlike 5.3.6 and unlike our own string.pack; the docs call the errors 5.3.6's without saying so
findings.claim: ob_err_type takes the type name from lj_typename(o), which never reads a metatable's __name. PUC 5.3.6 names the operand through luaT_objtypename (ltm.c), which uses a string __name from the metatable of a table or full userdata. Round 2's pk_typeerror (oclj_strpack.c:175-179) copies that behaviour for string.pack, so on this build pack and the operators now name the same value differently. Neither README.md:30 ("any other value, such as nil or a table, with 5.3.6's `attempt to perform bitwise operation on a nil value` (or `a table value`)") nor the round-3 roadmap row (docs/roadmap.md:208, "Errors are 5.3.6's ... with LuaJIT's word order where a variable is named") lists this difference. The only naming difference they list is the word order and "fewer operands named".
findings.failure_scenario: local t = setmetatable({}, {__name = 'Foo'}); return t | 1. Ours gives "attempt to perform bitwise operation on local 't' (a table value)". PUC 5.3.6 gives "attempt to perform bitwise operation on a Foo value (local 't')". The same holds for 1 << t, ~t, and a constructor used directly ("on a table value" here, "on a Foo value" there). By contrast, string.pack('i4', t) gives "got Foo" on both VMs.

[S] oclj_bitop_meta.c:95 (const char *tname = lj_typename(o)); 5.3.6 ldebug.c luaG_typeerror -> ltm.c luaT_objtypename; oclj_strpack.c:175-179 pk_typeerror reads __name. LuaJIT's arithmetic errors have the same gap, so this follows U5-A's "LuaJIT shape" and is not a wrong value. It is undocumented, though, and inconsistent with pack.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one. (a) Add one sentence to README.md:30 and roadmap row 208: the type name is LuaJIT's, so a metatable's __name is not used, where 5.3.6 and our string.pack use it. Optionally add a NAMING case to t_ops.lua with a deviations.txt entry. (b) Or, in ob_err_type, look up a string __name in the metatable of a table or userdata operand, as pk_typeerror does, before falling back to lj_typename. Use lj_meta_lookup or a raw lj_tab_getstr on the metatable, which allocates nothing before the error.

verdicts.title: Bitwise type error ignores __name, unlike 5.3.6 and our own string.pack; README.md:30 and roadmap row 208 don't list the difference
verdicts.evidence: [M] I wrote C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/r3/review2/verify-interp/name_probe.lua and ran it on r3/impl/A's luajit.exe (JIT on and -joff gave the same output) and on PUC 5.3.6 lua.exe, with CR stripped. With t = setmetatable({}, {__name='Foo'}): `t|1`, `1<<t` and `~t` give ours "attempt to perform bitwise operation on local 't' (a table value)" and PUC "... on a Foo value (local 't')". A constructor operand gives ours "on a table value" and PUC "on a Foo value". An upvalue gives ours "on upvalue 't' (a table value)" and PUC "on a Foo value (upvalue 't')". A non-string __name (42) falls back to "table" on both, so only the string case differs. string.pack('i4', t) gives "got Foo" on both VMs, which confirms the inconsistency with round 2. `t+1` shows the same gap in LuaJIT's own arithmetic error, so the behaviour follows U5-A (design.md:70-79: "LuaJIT's shape with 5.3's verb ... Every other operator error on this VM keeps LuaJIT's shape"). It is not a wrong value. [S] oclj_bitop_meta.c:95 ob_err_type: `const char *tname = lj_typename(o);`. PUC ltm.c:90-98 luaT_objtypename reads a string __name from the metatable of a table or full userdata. oclj_strpack.c:175-185 pk_typeerror calls luaL_getmetafield(L, arg, "__name"). [S] The docs leave it out: grep finds no '__name' in README.md, docs/*.md, test/native/bitop/deviations.txt, design.md or design-B.md. README.md:30 says "with 5.3.6's `attempt to perform bitwise operation on a nil value` (or `a table value`)", and that is false for a table whose metatable has a string __name. The only naming differences it lists are the word order and fewer operands named. Roadmap:208 says "Errors are 5.3.6's ... with LuaJIT's word order where a variable is named", with the same omission. No test covers a __name operand (t_ops.lua has no __name case), so nothing would catch a regression either way. The reach is narrow: Lua code must set a string __name on a metatable, and only the message text changes. That is why I rate it low, not medium.
verdicts.fix: Keep U5-A's behaviour, which matches LuaJIT's arithmetic errors, and document the deviation. Add one clause to README.md:30 after the word-order sentence and to roadmap row 208, for example: "and the type name is LuaJIT's, so a metatable's `__name` is not used (5.3.6 says `on a Foo value`, as `string.pack` does here, where this says `a table value`)". Optionally add a t_ops NAMING case with a deviations.txt entry so the difference is pinned. Changing ob_err_type to read __name (with lj_tab_getstr on the metatable, which allocates nothing) is the alternative. It would make bitwise errors name a value differently from arithmetic errors on the same VM, so the doc fix is the minimal one.

findings.title: The bitops gate's JIT loop cannot see what the compiled code computes before the raise, but its failure text says it catches that
findings.claim: The gate's hot()/cold() loop throws its running sum away when it raises at i = 151, so the gate's output depends only on where the loop raised and on the trace counts. It never depends on the values computed for i = 1..150. Despite that, the failure text (line 1195) says a hot field other than X>>@151 means the loop "computed something else before it", and the header (line 1108) says the loop computed the masked remedy "exactly 150 times". A JIT that gets the in-range values wrong but still raises at 151 passes the gate.
findings.failure_scenario: A build whose JIT computes wrong values for (-i & 0xFFFFFFFF) >> 8 & 0xFF or ((150 - i) >> 1) while i <= 150, but still exits its exactness guard at i = 151, prints exactly BO_WANT. negctl-bitop.sh's NARROW and KFOLD64 arms are examples: both miscompile in-range values, and that script's own catcher list gives only floor/fuzz for them, not the gate. Such a build passes build-native.sh. Only run-bitjit.sh and run-bitfuzz.sh, which are run by hand, would catch it.
findings.evidence: [S] Line 1147: hot() keeps s in a local and returns it only after the loop finishes; the raise at i = 151 discards it. E(hot) returns only the error kind, and same= (line 1167) compares only hres/cres and hlast/clast. [M] I took the gate probe out of build-native.sh unchanged and ran it on the built luajit.exe (C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/r3/impl/A/build/native/luajit-windows-x86_64/src): it prints BO_WANT. Then I changed only hot()'s remedy term to (i * 7), leaving cold() as it was (C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/r3/review2/review-plumbing/bitops-hotdiffers.lua). The output is still byte-identical to BO_WANT, including jit=1/0/0 and same=true. So the line cannot tell a compiled loop that computes other values from one that computes the right ones. [M] With the sum kept in an upvalue (sum150.lua), our build gives acc=43800 with the JIT on (-jv shows [TRACE 1 ... loop]) and under -joff. PUC 5.3.6 gives sum150=43800 (puc-twin.lua, which also reproduces every shared field of BO_WANT).
findings.suggested_fix: In hot() and cold(), store the running sum in an upvalue every iteration (acc = s after the add). Print it in the line (for example acc=43800, PUC 5.3.6's value for i = 1..150) and include it in same= (hacc == cacc). Then the hot field covers what its failure text promises. Otherwise, remove "or computed something else before it" and "exactly 150 times" from the failure text and the header, and say that the in-range values are run-bitjit.sh's job.

findings.title: A VM crash that cuts an ours file inside a tuple id ends the fuzz seed at 2 (PROVED NOTHING), not 1 as the comment promises
findings.claim: Lines 174-175 say a nonzero exit from our side is a failure 'whatever the compare said'. Line 176, `[ "$rj" -ne 0 ] || [ "$rf" -ne 0 ] && [ "$crc" -ne 2 ] && crc=1`, leaves crc at 2 whenever the comparator returned 2. The comparator returns 2 for exactly the cut a native crash tends to leave. bitfuzz.lua writes through a fully buffered io.open file, so the unflushed tail is lost and the file ends mid-line. If the cut falls in the first fields of a T line, bitfuzz-cmp.lua:112 calls die(2) ('desynchronised') before its own 'no #end: CRASH' check (line 148) is reached. If the cut falls later in the line, norm(nil) at bitfuzz-cmp.lua:54/117 throws a Lua error, so the 1 comes from the comparator crashing, not from its CRASH verdict.
findings.failure_scenario: A JIT bug segfaults luajit.exe during the ours JIT-on run, and the stdio buffer boundary falls inside 'T<TAB>125.16'. bitfuzz-cmp exits 2, rj is nonzero, and crc stays 2. The seed prints '2', and the run ends 'BITFUZZ PROVED NOTHING' (exit 2) instead of FAIL (exit 1). A crashing build gets triaged as an instrument problem.
findings.evidence: [M] I took a correct -joff ours file (seed 1, 300 cases) and cut it at 'T\t125' in tuple 2000: bitfuzz-cmp.lua exits 2 with 'desynchronised at tuple 2000 (125 vs 125.16)'. I cut it 30 characters into the same line: exit 1, but via a Lua traceback from norm (bitfuzz-cmp.lua:54). Line 176's logic evaluated with rj=1, crc=2 leaves crc=2. findings.title: run-bitjit.sh's ndiff counts only lines of 'got' missing from 'want': an empty or short JIT-on or PUC output that exits 0 counts as 0 differences

The generator's JIT-on runs, both PUC twins, the t_rec and t_jit2 option-set runs and t_jit2's PUC run (lines 196, 203, 254, 277, 286) have no line-count check. Only the -joff references do (lines 190 and 247). So a run that exits 0 with fewer lines, or none, compares equal.
findings.failure_scenario: A JIT-on drv.lua, t_rec.lua or t_jit2.lua run, or a PUC t_jit2 run, exits 0 having written only part of its lines, or nothing. findings.title: t_fold provenance cannot see three bare-literal LEX deviations: %.17g makes PUC's 2^53+1 and 2^63-1 print like ours, so deviations.txt omits them

findings.title: Round 3 breaks LuaJIT's bundled jit/bc.lua: a plain `luajit -jdump` stops most loops from compiling, and `luajit -bl` raises
findings.claim: jit.util.funcbc returns the 32-bit bytecode word as a signed int32 (lib_jit.c:220, setintV(L->top, ins)). The pinned jit/bc.lua decodes it with the native operators and assumes BitOp's 32-bit `>>`: line 68 `(ins >> 8) & 0xff`, line 73 `ins >> 16`, line 104 `ins >> 24`. Any word of 2^31 or more arrives negative. That covers every forward jump (D >= 0x8000, BCBIAS_J), every FORI and every negative KSHORT. Under round 3's 64-bit `>>` such a word gives a 56-bit result, which raises "result of '>>' has more than 53 significant bits". jit.dump's default modes include 'b' (dump.lua:681, `m = { t=true, b=true, i=true, m=true }`). Its record callback calls bcline for each recorded bytecode, so the error is thrown during recording and LuaJIT aborts the trace. [M][S]
findings.failure_scenario: p1.lua is a numeric for loop whose body has `t[1] or 3.0` (IST plus a forward JMP) and bit operators. `luajit -jdump p1.lua` on the round-3 build prints "VM handler failed: .\jit\bc.lua:68: result of '>>' has more than 53 significant bits" and "TRACE 1 abort ... error thrown or hook called during recording" three times, and the loop never compiles. `luajit -jv p1.lua` on the same file prints "[TRACE 1 p1.lua:4 loop]". The pristine tree's luajit.exe compiles it under -jdump. `luajit -bl p1.lua` lists 5 instructions, then dies with the same error at the FORI. Anyone diagnosing the JIT with the default -jdump, as docs/jit-guide.md (planned next) would likely recommend, sees bit-operator loops apparently refuse to compile. Secondary symptom: the gap that roadmap row 206 already records, where jit.util.tracek returns an unset value for KINT64 without FFI, is now hit in every bit-operator trace. Measured: tracek hands back the trace-number argument, so -jdump's IR shows `BAND 0025 +1` where the constant is 0x3FFFC (p7.lua: trace 1 -> 1, trace 2 -> 2).
findings.evidence: Scratch dir C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/r3/review2/review-jit/: p1.lua run under -jdump, -jdump=bitmsx, -jv and -bl in the built tree; p7.lua for tracek. jit/bc.lua there is byte-identical to the pristine tree's (CR stripped). grep of the built tree's jit/*.lua: bc.lua:67-119 and bcsave.lua:254,386 (`bswap(x) >> 16`) shift values that can be negative. dis_x86.lua shifts byte values only, and -jdump=m disassembled correctly. Not reachable inside the sandbox (no jit.* Lua modules there).

Either patch jit/bc.lua to decode with masks first (`(ins & 0xffffffff) >> 8`, or `ins % 2^32` before shifting, and the same at lines 73, 104 and 119), or make jit_util_funcbc return the word as an unsigned number (setnumV((lua_Number)ins)). At minimum, note in the roadmap and the JIT guide that -jdump needs `-jdump=-b` (or 'itmsx') on this build, and that its int64 constants are wrong.

findings.title: The width rule's written soundness argument says every outside value enters through a CONV scoring 64; int-typed values enter directly and score 33

All three are false for int-typed values. An int stack slot such as the narrowed loop index (SLOAD ... CI), or an int value replayed from a parent snapshot, reaches an int64 op directly or through CONV i64.int, and oclj_bitwidth scores it 33 (or 32/33 through the CONV), not 64. The conclusion still holds, because 33 is a property of the IR type, which loop_unroll keeps iteration-invariant. But the argument as written skips the one non-64 leaf that comes from outside. [M][S]

It would be reasoning from a false premise: outside ints already arrive without a num->i64 conversion. Measured: in p1.lua's trace, `0001 int SLOAD #4 CI` feeds `0016 i64 BXOR 0013 0001` directly (simplify_conv_sext's x64 LEFTFOLD removed the CONV i64.int). The README never links xorshift64 to the error, and so implies two wrong things: that bitwise-only 64-bit code is unaffected, and that the failure is a silently different value.

verdicts.title: Round 3 breaks LuaJIT's bundled jit/bc.lua: a plain `luajit -jdump` stops bit-operator loops from compiling, and `luajit -bl` raises
verdicts.evidence: [M] I copied review-jit/p1.lua to C:/Users/astro/claude-tmp/oclj/r3/review2/verify-jit/p1.lua and ran it in both trees. In the round-3 build, `luajit -jdump p1.lua` printed `VM handler failed: .\jit\bc.lua:68: result of '>>' has more than 53 significant bits` and `TRACE 1 abort p1.lua:5 -- error thrown or hook called during recording` three times, and the loop never compiled. `-jv` on the same build printed `[TRACE 1 p1.lua:4 loop]`. `-bl` listed 0001-0005, then died at the FORI with the same error. The pristine tree's luajit.exe compiled the loop under -jdump (`TRACE 1 stop -> loop`) and listed all 22 instructions under -bl. Both trees printed 154576. [S] The built tree's jit/bc.lua is byte-identical to the pristine one once CR is stripped (diff). lib_jit.c:220 jit_util_funcbc does `setintV(L->top, ins)`, so any word with bit 31 set (a forward jump or FORI, whose D carries BCBIAS_J, or a negative KSHORT) arrives negative. Under round 3, `ins >> 8` on such a word is 56 bits, so it raises (bc.lua:68). `ins >> 16` (lines 73 and 119) and `ins >> 24` (line 104) give 48- and 40-bit values: they do not raise but are silently wrong. Line 68 runs first in bcline, which is why the failure shows up as a raise. [M] Masking first (`ins & 0xffffffff`, then shifting) gives the same op, A, B and D in both trees (fixprobe.lua; fix-r3.txt and fix-pristine.txt are identical, including the 4 negative words). Scope corrections: (a) the bcsave.lua:254/386 `bswap(x) >> 16` sites cannot be reached on this build. They sit behind `ffi.abi(...)`, and `-b -t obj` already fails with "FFI library required to write this file type" because FFI is off (round 1), not because of round 3 [M]. (b) The tracek KINT64 symptom is the gap already recorded in roadmap row 206 (`jit.util.tracek returns an unset value for a KINT64 constant`), not new [S]. The p7 measurement (tracek returns the trace number) does reproduce [M]. (c) No repo gate is affected. build-native.sh, run-bit*.sh, p4v.lua, t_fold.lua, penalty_test.lua and m3.lua decode funcbc with `% 256` or bit.band and never call bc.lua, -jdump or -b [S, grep]. This is developer tooling only, and the sandbox has no jit.* modules. Still, the default diagnostic instrument now changes what the JIT does (traces abort), with docs/jit-guide.md planned next. [S, additional] jit/dump.lua:368 `sn >> 24` decodes tracesnap entries, which lib_jit.c:359 also passes as (int32_t). A slot of 128 or more yields a 40-bit value, so that slot prints as `----`. No raise. Rare.
verdicts.fix: Preferred, one line in the build copy via a bitop patch: lib_jit.c jit_util_funcbc, `setintV(L->top, ins)` -> `setnumV(L->top, (lua_Number)(uint32_t)ins)`. Then every bc.lua shift is exact, and the repo's own funcbc readers (`% 256`, bit.band) are unaffected. Optionally do the same for tracesnap's map entries (lib_jit.c:359-360) so dump.lua's `sn >> 24` stays right for slots of 128 or more. Alternative: patch the build copy's jit/bc.lua to mask first, `local u = ins & 0xffffffff`, and use u at lines 68, 73, 104 and 119 (measured equivalent). At minimum, record in roadmap row 208, and later in the JIT guide, that -jdump on this build needs `-jdump=itmsx` (no 'b') and that -bl fails. Drop bcsave.lua from the fix: it is unreachable without FFI.

verdicts.title: The width rule's written soundness argument says every outside value enters through a CONV scoring 64; int-typed values enter directly and score 33
verdicts.evidence: [M] In my run of `-jdump=itmsx` on p1.lua in the round-3 build (verify-jit/p1-itmsx.txt, colours stripped), `0001 int SLOAD #4 CI` is a stack-slot value from outside the trace, and it feeds `0016 i64 BXOR 0013 0001` directly, with no CONV i64.num. In the loop copy, `0034 i64 BXOR 0028 0026` (0028 is `int ADD 0001 +1`, 0026 is `BAND ... +k`) is followed by no EQ.i64 guard. The pre-roll's 0016, whose other operand is the CONV i64.num of a num SLOAD, keeps its guard 0019. [S] oclj_bitop_fold.c:60 `if (irt_isint(ir->t)) return 33;` scores such a leaf 33, and :63-65 scores CONV i64.int 32 or 33. So the premise at oclj_bitop_fold.c:35-37 is false as written ("every value that enters the trace from outside it ... reaches an int64 op through CONV i64.num of a double, which scores 64"). So is its repetition in roadmap row 208 ("every value from outside enters through a conversion the bound scores 64"). patch-bitop-fold.sh:50-53 says outside values "arrive as plain doubles", but the point that rule needs (never a marked conversion) still holds. The patch's own comment in simplify_conv_i64_num (build copy lj_opt_fold.c, about line 1155) already names the case: "an int-typed y is the int loop index after simplify_conv_sext's x64 LEFTFOLD". [I] The conclusion survives, and I could not turn this into a wrong value. Any int-typed IR value is an int32, sign- or zero-extended, so it lies within 33 bits whatever its origin. Its type is iteration-invariant (lj_opt_loop.c:343-352). So the bound of 33 depends on no carried value. This is purely a misstated proof premise.
verdicts.fix: Reword oclj_bitop_fold.c:35-37 and roadmap row 208 to: every value from outside the trace enters either as a double, through CONV i64.num, which scores 64, or as an int-typed value (a narrowed SLOAD such as the loop index, or an int from a parent snapshot). The int value scores 33 (32 sign-extended through CONV i64.int) from its type alone, and IR types are iteration-invariant. In patch-bitop-fold.sh:52, change "arrive as plain doubles" to "arrive as plain doubles or ints".

verdicts.title: README line 32 lists xorshift64 as an algorithm that 'adds or multiplies between' the operators; it only xors and shifts, and it raises the 53-bit error
verdicts.evidence: [S] README.md:32: 'a 64-bit algorithm that adds or multiplies between them (xorshift64, a 64-bit hash, SHA-512) cannot match 5.3'. [M] My probe r3/review2/verify-docs/xs64.lua runs xorshift64 13/7/17 from seed 1, with only ~, << and >>. On the A build's luajit.exe, step 1 gives 1082269761 and step 2 raises "result of '~' has more than 53 significant bits". PUC 5.3.6 continues: 1.1529929988338534e+18, -7.2692274092767867e+18, and so on. The cause given for xorshift64 is false. The conclusion, 'cannot match 5.3', is true, and README:28 already says that a result over 53 bits raises. So this is a wrong reason, not a wrong statement about what happens: low, not medium.

verdicts.title: Row 146 says the operators compute Lua 5.3.6's 64-bit results 'again'; no earlier build computed 5.3.6's results
verdicts.evidence: [S] Pristine tree prototype/watchdog/luajit/src/lj_meta.c lj_meta_bitop:245-281 (LJ_HASFFI). With a cdata operand (id != 0), shifts go through lj_carith_shift64. lj_carith.c:294-296 masks the count with `sh&63`, so `1LL << 64` is 1LL where 5.3.6 gives 0, and a negative count shifts by (c&63) instead of the other way. Results were cdata (`1099511627776LL`), not numbers. With number operands (:265-272, :280) the results were always 32-bit (`setintV(ra, (int32_t)b)`). lj_opt_fold.c:380-382 also uses `k2 & 63`. The row's own 2026-10-16 sentence says the earlier 64-bit form was the cdata `1LL << 40`. So the operators never computed 5.3.6's 64-bit results before round 3, and 'again' is false. The harm is only a historical misreading.
verdicts.fix: docs/roadmap.md row 146: delete 'again', or write '... now compute Lua 5.3.6's 64-bit integer results on plain numbers, which no earlier build did (before FFI was removed, only cdata operands were 64-bit, by FFI's rules)'.

verdicts.title: Row 206 says BitOp leaves a 'result' beyond ±2^51 unspecified; it is an operand beyond ±2^51 whose conversion is unspecified
verdicts.evidence: [S] docs/roadmap.md row 206 ('Found 2026-10-17'): 'BitOp leaves a result beyond ±2^51 unspecified and LuaJIT's narrowing exploits that'. BitOp's results are always signed 32-bit (pristine lj_meta.c:280 `setintV(ra, (int32_t)b)`), so no result can lie beyond ±2^51. The repo's own text gets it right. native/luajit/patch-bitop-record.sh:20: 'BitOp leaves operands beyond +-2^51 unspecified'. test/native/bitop/t_bit.lua:15: 'Operands stay within +-2^51'. In the example, the operand i*2^45 - i passes 2^51 from i = 65 (the reviewer's 'i >= 64' is off by one, which does not matter). This is wording only.
verdicts.fix: docs/roadmap.md row 206: 'BitOp leaves the conversion of an operand beyond ±2^51 unspecified, and LuaJIT's narrowing exploits that, ...'.

verdicts.title: Row 210 says round 3 raises the type error 'exactly where 5.3 would look for a metamethod'; 5.3.6 also looks for one where round 3 raises 'no integer representation'
verdicts.evidence: [S] bench/vendor/lua-5.3.6/src/lvm.c, OP_BAND..OP_BNOT: if tointeger fails for either operand, they call luaT_trybinTM. ltm.c luaT_trybinTM raises tointerror only after the metamethod lookup fails. With getmetatable('').__bor set, PUC gives `'1.5' | 0` -> 'string __bor called'; LuaJIT gives 'number has no integer representation'.
